title: Show 2D Puckerings
content: **Show 2D Puckering** \- Show Puckerings in the 2D window even when Puckering tools are not in use. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022664487/mceclip0.png) **Show 2D Puckerings** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to and select Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Materials ▶ **Show 2D Puckerings ** \- When the **Show 2D Puckerings** is activated, all Puckering lines will show and disappear from the 2D window.

title: Change Length
content: **Change Length** \- Change the length of a segment towards the start, end, or both directions. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022574087/mceclip0.png) **Edit Pattern** tool. Navigate to the 2D window, right click on a segment to be edited and select **Change Length.** The Change Length window will appear. \- Select and modify below settings as needed. * * **Start \- **Follow the instruction above to open the Change Length Window. \- For Location, select **Start.** Then, type in the desired value to **Length.** \- The start point of the selected segment will be adjusted based on the designated length value. * **End ** \- Follow the instruction above to open the Change Length window. \- For Location, select **End.** Then, type in the desired value to **Length.** \- The end point of the selected segment will be adjusted based on the designated length value. * **Both** \- Follow the instruction above to open the Change Length window. \- For Location, select **Both.** Then, type in the desired value to **Length.** \- Both start and end points of the selected segment will be equally adjusted based on the designated length value.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide on how to change the length of a segment in the 2D window using the Edit Pattern tool in CLO 3D.

title: The patterns are deformed when I import my DXF file into CLO. How can I fix the problem?
content: **Question** When I import my DXF file into CLO selecting the 'Swap Cutting line and Sewing Line' setting, some of the patterns are deformed. How can I fix the problem? Example of deformation of a pattern: ![DXF1.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360058514333/DXF1.jpg) **Answer** The problem may occur when creating a pattern from 2D CAD software. Please firstly check two things below: 1. **If a sewing line or a cutting line of a pattern is made as 'Baseline' from 2D CAD program: ** If a pattern is created with 'Baselines' from 2D CAD program, the pattern might not be compatible with CLO. For patterns to be imported into CLO, it is recommended to create it with 'Outlines' instead of 'Baselines'. 2. **If a pattern is created as an unclosed shape from 2D CAD program:** If a pattern is created as an unclosed shape from 2D CAD program, it might not be compatible with CLO. The feature named 'Swap Cutting line and Sewing line' is for importing a pattern into CLO by swapping sewing lines and cutting lines. However, as for patterns created as an unclosed shape, some of the patterns may be deformed when imported into CLO with 'Swap Cutting line and Sewing line'. Thus, please firstly make sure whether a pattern is created as an unclosed shape or not. And if the former, modify the pattern to a closed shape and try to import it into CLO again. ![DXF2.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360058514313/DXF2.jpg)
content_description: This web page provides troubleshooting tips for resolving pattern deformation issues when importing DXF files into CLO using the 'Swap Cutting line and Sewing Line' setting.

title: Surface Tape Measurement
content: **List of Contents** Surface Tape Measurement Measure Length **Surface Tape Measurement** \- Measure specific length of the Avatar, arm length and back length, by going over the curves of the Avatar’s surface. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022743447/mceclip3.png) **Surface Tape Measurement** tool from the 3D Toolbar by holding down the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022804688/mceclip0.png) Basic Tape Measurement tool for more than two seconds or navigate to and select Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Measurement ▶ **Surface Tape Measurement.** ** Measure Length** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022743447/mceclip3.png) **Surface Tape Measurement** tool from the 3D Toolbar by holding down the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022804688/mceclip0.png) **Basic Tape Measurement** tool for more than two seconds. \- Click on the Avatar to create the start point. \- Drag the mouse as an orange line and point follow along the mouse. \- Double click on the Avatar to complete the length measurement. \- When the length is measured properly, the line will be highlighted in yellow and the measurement will appear next to the line. title: Internal Polygon/Line
content: **List of Contents** Internal Polygon Create Internal Shape Create Internal Shapes with Curves Create Internal Lines with Specific Values Create Internal Lines Create Points in Guidelines Cancel the Last Action Cancel All Actions **Internal Polygon** \- Create Internal Lines and Internal Shapes within Patterns. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022400307/mceclip0.png) **Internal Polygon/Line** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select 2D pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Internal Polygon/Line.** ** Create Internal Shape** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022400307/mceclip0.png) **Internal Polygon/Line** tool and click within the Pattern to draw desired shape of Internal Shape. \- Click the start point again to complete the Internal Shape. **Create Internal Shapes with Curves** \- Hold down the Ctrl key while clicking within the Pattern to create curves with the free curve point. \- Or, click and drag the mouse while adding a point within the Pattern to create curves with AI Bezier handles. **Create Internal Lines with Specific Values** \- Click and then right click within the Pattern to access the Create Internal Polygon window. \- Type in the desired values to Length and Position. **Create Internal Lines** \- Click to create a start point. \- Continue to click to make the desired shape of an Internal Line. \- Double click to complete. **Create Points in Guidelines** \- Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to add points in a straight line or a diagonal line. **Cancel the Last Action** \- While creating the Internal Lines or Shapes, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action. **Cancel All Actions** \- While creating the Internal Lines or Shapes, hit the Esc or Ctrl+Z keys on the keyboard to cancel all actions. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for users to effectively create and manage internal shapes and lines within patterns using the Internal Polygon/Line tool in Clo3D.

title: HASP Error Message
content: **List of Contents** Communication error between local and remote Sentinel HASP License Managers (H0040) Feature not found (H0031) Sentinel HASP key not found (H0007) Too many concurrent useres (H0038) Unable to access Sentinel HASP Run-time Environment(H0033) **Communication error between local and remote Sentinel HASP License Managers (H0040)** **Cause of Error** The Server and Client PCs are unable to communicate with each other. **Solution** 1. Type 'services.msc' in the Run window. ![1.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360077798874/1.jpg) 2. In the Service window that follows, check whether or not the status of the ‘Sentinel LDK License Manager’ is ‘Running’. If the status is not ‘Running’, right click and select **Start**. If the status is ‘Started’, right click and select **Restart**. Reboot. ![33.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000410167/33.png) 3. If this does not solve the problem, check both versions of the Server and Client PC’s HASP Drivers. Make sure both versions are the same. You are able to check the version under Diagnostics. ![image.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360077799894/image.png) 4. If this does not work, ask your Network Administrator to confirm the Port communication status between the Server and Client. Check whether the 1947 Port is being used by another program. **Feature not found (H0031)** **Cause of Error** Despite the dongle key has been recognized, the Feature ID of the program and the Feature ID of the dongle key are different. (This occurs when the wrong version of CLO 3D is installed - i.e. installed the Stand-Alone version for a Network dongle key, and vice versa) **Solution** Make sure the correct version of CLO 3D is installed. ex> Purchased the Network version, but used the Stand-Alone version's installer. -> Re-install CLO 3D using the Network version's installer. **Sentinel HASP key not found (H0007)** **Objective** **Cause of Error** \- When the HASP Key is not plugged in to the PC. \- Network Version only: the Client PC does not recognize the Server PC that the dongle key is connected to. \- When the HASP Key is recognized, but the Sentinel License Manager service fails to start properly. **Solution** Make sure the HASP is connected to the PC. 1. Check the red light of the HASP Key. It should light up when plugged in to the PC. 2. Check whether or not the HASP Key shows up in the [ACC page](http://localhost:1947/) (refer to the image below). ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115000784388/Sentinel_HASP_key_not_found__H0007_.png) 3. If the red light, or the ACC page does not look equal to the image above, refer to the following manual, reinstall the Sentinel HASP Driver. [Sentinel HASP Driver Manual Installation](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000558507-%EC%84%A4%EC%B9%98-%ED%9B%84-%EB%B0%9C%EC%83%9D%ED%95%A0-%EC%88%98-%EC%9E%88%EB%8A%94-%EB%AC%B8%EC%A0%9C-%ED%95%B4%EA%B2%B0-%EB%B0%8F-%EB%B0%A9%EB%B2%95) **Too many concurrent users (H0038)** **Cause of Error** When the number of users connected to the program exceeds the maximum allowed number of users. ex> If the maximum number of users (the number of purchased licenses) is 2, and 3 users try to log-in, the last person to attempt a connection will receive an error message. **Solution** Check the number of current users via the link below. Connect when one of the current users exit the program. [ACC Page ](http://localhost:1947/) Click **Sentinel Keys** , on the left. When the Key shows up as the image above, click **Sessions** , on the right. The following page should display the current user(s). Connect when one of the current users exits the program. If any unauthorized user is connected, click the **Disconnect** button on the right to log the person out of the program. **Unable to access Sentinel HASP Run-time Environment(H0033)** **Cause of Error** The HASP Driver has not been properly installed on the PC, or the Driver is damaged. To confirm whether it being properly installed, enter [http://localhost:1947](http://localhost:1947/) or [http://127.0.0.1:1947](http://127.0.0.1:1947%EC%9D%84/) into your web browser, or click on the following link ( [ACC Page](http://127.0.0.1:1947/) ). If the following page does not look equal to the image below, there is a problem with the Sentinel HASP Driver. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115000736287/Unable_to_access_Sentinel_HASP_Run-time_Environment_H0033_.png) **Solution** Refer to the following manual and reinstall the HASP Driver. [HASP Driver Installation ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000558507-%EC%84%A4%EC%B9%98-%ED%9B%84-%EB%B0%9C%EC%83%9D%ED%95%A0-%EC%88%98-%EC%9E%88%EB%8A%94-%EB%AC%B8%EC%A0%9C-%ED%95%B4%EA%B2%B0-%EB%B0%8F-%EB%B0%A9%EB%B2%95) Go Back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides troubleshooting solutions for common errors encountered with Sentinel HASP License Managers, ensuring users can resolve issues efficiently and maintain seamless access to their software.

title: How can I join CLO Discord?
content: **Account Creation** * Go to [https://discord.com/](https://discord.com/) * Create an account * Choose how you want to access Discord * Option 1: Choose to download the Discord app for your desktop * Option 2: Choose to access Discord in your browser **Joining the CLO Discord Server** * Copy the CLO Discord server invitation link to your Clipboard * <https://bit.ly/CLOOFFICIAL> * Open the Discord Desktop App * Click on the Add a Server Button on the left side of the interface ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/7814772432921) * In the **Create a Server** Pop-up, Click **Join a Server** at the bottom ![mceclip1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/7814776251033) * Paste the server link in the**Invite Link** field, then click**Join Server ![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/7814830874649) ** * The CLO icon will now appear on the left side of your interface. ![mceclip3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/7814848111897) * Go to the **Notice** channels on the left side. Please read the **Rules** and **Read me First** text channels ![mceclip4.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/7814904331289) * Go to the **Self-Roles** channel and react with the blue dot to gain full access to all of the CLO channels ![mceclip5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/7814874720281) ![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/7814908382617) * You will now see all of the different CLO text channels. Happy CLOing!
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for creating a Discord account and joining the CLO Discord server to enhance your community experience.

title: Shape Dart Cap
content: **Shape Dart Cap** \- Smooth Pattern outlines with darts. \- Select the ![edit_pattern.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001809048/edit_pattern.png)**Edit Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar. ** ** \- Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard and select two segments forming darts. \- Right-click on the select segments and select **Shape Dart Cap** from the pop-up menu. \- A black line appears showing how Pattern would look when darts are sewn. -Click and drag the red point on the black line to modify the curve as needed and hit the Enter key on the keyboard. \- Pattern outlines with the dart are edited based on the modification. \- Dart’s folded Pattern outlines appear as Baselines.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for using the Shape Dart Cap tool to edit pattern outlines with darts in your design software.

title: Show Grading
content: **List of Contents** Show Grading Show/hide Size Group Show/hide All Grading **Show Grading** \- Show or hide grading from the 2D Patterns. \- Show/hide Size Group Object Browser ▶ Grading Tab ▶ Size Group (Select Desired) ▶ Property Editor ▶ **Show** Show/hide All Grading 2D Toolbar ▶ ![showhide_grading.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001182908/showhide_grading.png)**Show Grading** Main Menu ▶ Show ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ **Show Grading** **Show/Hide Size Group** \- To show or hide specific Size Group, click the desired Size Group from the Object Browser ▶Grading Tab. \- Toggle off the Show option to hide the selected Size Group. \- Toggle on to show the Size Group again. **Show/Hide All Grading** \- To show or hide all grading, click the ![showhide_grading.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001182908/showhide_grading.png)**Show Grading** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- All grading in the 2D window disappears. \- Click the ![showhide_grading.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001182908/showhide_grading.png)**Show Grading** tool again to appear all grading. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides instructions on how to show or hide grading and size groups within the 2D Patterns of the CLO 3D design software.

title: History Window
content: **List of Contents** 3D State Delete & Rename **Objective ** Keep track of your workflow with the History window and revert to previous points at any given time. In addition, save 3D states to review and compare specific points of progress. ** Location** **3D State** History Window ▶ **3D State** **Delete & Rename** Right-click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D State) ▶ **Delete or Rename** ** Operation** **3D State** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: History Window ▶ **3D State** 2. Double click the desired 3D State. → Warning as follows appears: "Loading the 3D State will delete the current History. Would you like to proceed?" 3. Select OK. → The 3D garment is reverted to the selected 3D State. **Delete & Rename** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right-click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D State) ▶ **Delete or Rename** → The name field is highlighted and name can be changed. → The selected 3D State is deleted. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides guidance on managing 3D states, including how to track workflow history, revert to previous states, and delete or rename specific 3D states.

title: Delete Buttonhole Style
content: ### **Objective** Delete unnecessary buttonhole styles. ### **Location** Object Browser ▶ Buttonhole Tab **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Buttonhole Tab** ** 2. Select a buttonhole style to be deleted. 3. Press the Delete key on keyboard or right click on the buttonhole style and select **Delete**. → The selected buttonhole style is deleted.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide a step-by-step guide for deleting unnecessary buttonhole styles from the Object Browser's Buttonhole Tab.

title: Menu
content: The Main Menu is located on the topmost left of the CLO 3D Modelist, and a pop-up menu can be launched by right clicking in the 3D Garment Window and the 2D Pattern Window for fast access to each function. The 3D Environment Pop-up Menu, the Avatar Pop-up Menu, and the Garment Pop-up Menu can be launched from the 3D Avatar Window, and the Pattern Edit Pop-up Menu, the Pattern, Line/Point, Seam Line Pop-up Menu, etc. can be launched from the 2D Pattern Window. **Main Menu ** Located on the topmost left of the CLO 3D Modelist, it shows the menus for each function. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115000446147/04_____.png) ※Note: Use the **Help** menu to navigate to our [Help Center](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/) with program manuals, online lessons, FAQ, community and more with tremendous helpful resources (ver5.0.0.)
content_description: Explore the functionality of the CLO 3D Modelist with quick access to various menus through both the Main Menu and pop-up options in the 3D Garment and 2D Pattern Windows.

title: Add Point/Split Line
content: **Objective** Add points and split a segment into multiple segments. Just simply click or enter values to add points on segments. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Add Point/Split Line** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001143328/______.png) **Add Point/Split Line** **Operation** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated. 2. Move the mouse cursor over the segment. → Smart Guide is displayed and the mouse cursor snaps at the intersection with the segment. (ver 7.0) 3. Click the segment where the point is to be added. → Point is added at the segment 4. Or right click on a line. → Split Line window appears 5. Set the option ****** ****** **Split into****Two lines** | Adjust by entering the length of both lines which are divided by the right clicked point, or by entering the ratio. ---|--- **Split****by Length** | Enter the number of segments the selected line should be divided into. You can change the direction in which a point is added to a start/opposite/center basis. **Uniform****split** | Enter the number of segments the line should be divided into. The line is equally divided accordingly. **※Note:** Use the Edit pattern to tool Select multiple segments and right click ▶When you select **Split** select, additional points can be added to multiple segments as they are detected as a single line.
content_description: This web page provides a guide on how to easily add points and split segments in a 2D pattern using the designated tools and options.

title: Show 2D Topstitches
content: **Show 2D Topstitches ** **-** Show or hide Topstitches in the 2D window at your convenience. \- Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Materials ▶ **Show 2D Topstitches.** \- 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Toolbar_Common_Stitch_View.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001177088/Toolbar_Common_Stitch_View.png)**Show 2D Topstitches.** \- Click the ![Toolbar_Common_Stitch_View.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001177088/Toolbar_Common_Stitch_View.png)**Show 2D Topstitches** tool from the 2D toolbar to hide Topstitches from the 2D Patterns. \- To show Topstitches again, click the Show 2D Topstitches tool again.
content_description: Easily manage the visibility of Topstitches in your 2D window with the Show 2D Topstitches feature, accessible through the Main Menu or 2D Toolbar.

title: Copy/Save Current V-Ray Render Image
content: **List of Contents** Copy/Save Current Image Copy Current Image Save Current Image Show in Saved Folder **Copy/Save Current Image **\- Simply copy or save the image appears in the preview window to quickly utilize rendered images. * **Copy Current Image** \- Select the![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026411567/mceclip0.png) **Copy Current Image** tool from the Render toolbar. * **Save Current Image** \- Select the![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026454208/mceclip2.png) **Save Current Image** tool from the Render toolbar. ** Copy Current Image ** \- Select the![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026411567/mceclip0.png) **Copy Current image** tool to copy the current preview image shown in the Render window. \- The image is copied to the clipboard and can be pasted into another program. **Save Current Image ** \- Select the![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026454208/mceclip2.png) **Save Current Image** tool to save the current preview image shown in the Render window. \- The Save Image File window appears allowing you to locate the saving path. \- Name the file and locate the saving path and click Save. \- The image is saved. **Show in Saved Folder ** \- To see saved images, click the![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026454368/mceclip3.png) **Show in Saved Folder** tool from the Render toolbar. \- The folder located in the saving path assigned in the Image/Video Properties appears, showing saved render outputs. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to copy, save, and access rendered images from the preview window.

title: Select Mesh (Lasso)
content: **List of Conetens** Select Mesh (Lasso) Select Multiple Areas Delete Selection Invert Selection Select a Segment Select a Pattern **Select Mesh(Box) ** \- Select and move 3D Garment mesh as needed. \- Hold down the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022721948/mceclip0.png) **Select Mesh (Box)** tool on the 3D toolbar to access the child menus. Then, select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022723088/mceclip0.png) **Select Mesh (Box)** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select 3D Garment ▶ **Select Mesh (Lasso).** ** Select Multiple Areas** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022723088/mceclip0.png) Select Mesh (Lasso) tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Patterns in the 2D window and 3D window will appear in yellow-green Mesh structure. \- Click and drag on the Pattern to freehand Lasso selection as desired to select desired area. \- Hold down the Shift and Ctrl keys on the keyboard to select multiple areas on the 3D Garment. **Delete Selection** \- To deselect particular areas, hold down the Ctrl key on the keyboard and click and drag to encompass the desired area in the 2D window. The encompassed area will be deselected. **Invert Selection** \- To invert the selection, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to click and drag on the 3D Garment. \- The areas originally not selected will be selected and vice-versa. \- The selected area will be highlighted in yellow-green. **Select a Segment** \- Double click on the Pattern outline in the 2D or 3D window to select a segment. **Select a Pattern** \- Double click within the Pattern in the 2D or 3D window to select a Pattern. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on utilizing selection tools for manipulating 3D garment meshes in CLO 3D, including options for lasso, box selection, and segment manipulation.

title: Fit Map
content: **List of Contents** Fit Map Can't Wear vs. Tight **Fit Map** \- Check the tightness of 3D Garments with the color scale. \- Hover over the third icon in the Vertical View Toggle Menu in the 3D window and select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022307467/mceclip1.png) **Fit Map** icon. ** Can't Wear vs. Tight** \- When the **Fit Map** icon is selected, the 3D Garment will appear in white, yellow, and red, each indicating the tightness of the 3D Garment. \- Red shows the **Cant’ Wear** areas on the 3D Garment, where the Garment is too tight, not possible to wear in real life. \- The percentage of the Can’t Wear areas will show on the Can’t Wear box’s right. \- Yellow shows the **Tight** areas on the 3D Garment, where the Garment is tight. \- The percentage of the Tight areas will show on the Tight box’s right. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: Explore the Fit Map feature to assess the tightness of 3D garments, visually represented through a color scale that highlights areas that are too tight or simply snug.

title: Edit UV
content: **Edit UV** \- Change the Pattern placement and edit the UV layout in the 2D Window. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022193908/mceclip0.png) **Edit** **UV** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to and select Main Menu ▶ Material ▶ **Edit** **UV.** * **Automatic \- **The **Automatic** option is set as default. \- When the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022193908/mceclip0.png) **Edit** **UV** tool’s setting is set as Automatic, the UV area will be automatically assigned, surrounding all Patterns in the 2D window. * **Manual ** \- The marquee box surrounding all Patterns in the 2D window will appear when the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022193908/mceclip0.png)**Edit UV** tool is activated. \- Click the icon on the right top of the marquee box. \- The ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022193908/mceclip0.png)**Edit UV** tool’s setting will be changed to Manual, allowing users to manually edit the UV area. \- When the marquee box changes to light blue, click and drag the marquee box to resize the UV area. \- Select and move the Patterns to rearrange them within the UV area.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for using the Edit UV tool in the 2D window to modify pattern placement and UV layouts in a user-friendly manner.
